```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r, results='hide'}
Data <- read.csv("WA_Fn-UseC_-HR-Employee-Attrition.csv")

#Understanding the Data
str(Data)
summary(Data)

colSums(is.na(Data))
#Data has no missing or null value.
```

```{r}
#Preparing the Data

#Converting the Target Variable (Attrition) from Character(Yes/No) to Factor(1/0)
Data$Attrition <- ifelse(Data$Attrition == "Yes", 1, 0)

#Removing the unnecessary columns which we are not using for prediction.
Data$EmployeeCount <- NULL
Data$Over18 <- NULL
Data$StandardHours <- NULL
Data$EmployeeNumber <- NULL

#Converting all character columns to factor.
Data <- data.frame(lapply(Data, function(x) {
  if(is.character(x)) as.factor(x) else x
}))

#Splitting the data into Training (80% of data) and Testing (20% of data) sets so we can check how well the model performs on new unseen data. This will also avoid overfitting.
library(caret)

set.seed(123)

trainIndex <- createDataPartition(Data$Attrition, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)

train <- Data[trainIndex, ]
test <- Data[-trainIndex, ]
```

```{r}
#Applying Machine Learning Models and Comparing.

#Logistic Regression 
#This model predicts whether an employee will leave (Attrition = 1) or stay (Attrition = 0)

model_log <- glm(Attrition ~ ., data = train, family = "binomial")

#Prediction
pred_log <- predict(model_log, test, type = "response")

#Converting probabilities into YES/NO.
pred_class <- ifelse(pred_log > 0.5, 1, 0) #if probability is > 50%, it predicts that employee will leave.

#Confusion Matrix of Logistic Regression
confusionMatrix(as.factor(pred_class), as.factor(test$Attrition))

#Random Forest
#Building Random Forest which usually improves prediction of attrition.
library(randomForest)
model_rf <- randomForest(as.factor(Attrition) ~ ., data = train)
pred_rf <- predict(model_rf, test)

#Confution Matrix of Random Forest
confusionMatrix(pred_rf, as.factor(test$Attrition))

#Accuracy of Random Forest is 85.71%, where for Logistic Regression is 89.8%, which means Logistic Regression model performs better than Random Forest for our dataset.

#Variable Importance/ Key Drivers
varImp(model_rf)

#Final Results:
#The Logistic Regression model performed better than Random Forest, achieving an accuracy of 89.8% in predicting employee attrition. The results show that factors such as overtime, frequent business travel, and long distance from home increase attrition, while job satisfaction and work-life balance help reduce it. Management can use these insights to improve employee retention and reduce turnover.

```
